title: First Amended Petition to Contest Will and for Declaratory Judgment
text:
IN THE PROBATE COURT NO. 1 OF HARRIS COUNTY, TEXAS

IN THE ESTATE OF
MARGARET ROSELLI O’CONNOR, DECEASED

CAUSE NO. 2024-PR-03821

FIRST AMENDED PETITION TO CONTEST WILL AND FOR DECLARATORY JUDGMENT

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

COMES NOW, CLIENT LYDIA ANNE ROSSELLI, individually and as independent executrix of the estate of Margaret Roselli O’Connor, deceased, and files this First Amended Petition to Contest Will and for Declaratory Judgment, and in support thereof respectfully shows the Court as follows:

I. PARTIES

1. Plaintiff, Lydia Anne Rosselli (also known as Lydia A. Rosselli, Lydia Rosselli, and familiarly as “Liddy”), is an individual resident of Harris County, Texas. Her date of birth is February 14, 1980. Her Social Security number is 456 78 9012. She may be served with process at her counsel’s address below.

2. Defendant, Elena Marie O’Connor-Wallace (formerly known as Elena Marie O’Connor, maiden name O’Connor), is an individual resident of Dallas County, Texas. She is the opposing party in this matter, contesting the validity of the Last Will and Testament of Margaret Roselli O’Connor dated March 15, 2023. Her Social Security number is 987-65-4321. Her telephone number is 713-555-0198. Her email address is e.oconnor-wallace@emaildomain.com.

3. Counsel for Plaintiff: John T. Harrington, Attorney at Law, Harrington & Associates, PLLC, 100 Main Street, Suite 300, Houston, Texas 77002. Telephone: 713-555-0142. Email: j.harrington@harringtonlaw.com.

4. Counsel for Defendant: Sarah M. Kline, Kline & Boyd, LLP, 2000 Commerce Drive, Dallas, Texas 75201.

5. The Honorable Patricia R. Nguyen is the judge presiding over this probate matter.

II. JURISDICTION AND VENUE

6. This Court has jurisdiction pursuant to Tex. Est. Code § 55.001 et seq. and Tex. Prob. Code § 5(b) (now codified in the Estates Code). Venue is proper because decedent Margaret Roselli O’Connor was a resident of Harris County at the time of her death.

III. FACTUAL BACKGROUND

7. Decedent Margaret Roselli O’Connor died on October 12, 2024, leaving a purported Last Will and Testament dated March 15, 2023 (the “2023 Will”). Plaintiff Lydia Rosselli, decedent’s daughter, is named as independent executrix and primary beneficiary. Defendant Elena O’Connor-Wallace, decedent’s other daughter, contests the 2023 Will on grounds of undue influence and lack of testamentary capacity.

8. A.B., a minor child, is the daughter of Plaintiff and is a contingent beneficiary under the 2023 Will. In re A.B., 678 S.W.3d 234 (Tex. App.—Houston [1st Dist.] 2023) is cited for the proposition that a minor’s interest must be protected by a guardian ad litem. Additionally, the court in Rosselli v. O’Connor, 456 S.W.3d 789 (Tex. 2024) addressed similar undue influence claims. This Court is also guided by In re Estate of Carmichael, 123 S.W.3d 456 (Tex. 2003).

IV. CAUSES OF ACTION

9. Plaintiff seeks a declaratory judgment that the 2023 Will is valid and that the alleged earlier will dated June 1, 2019 (the “2019 Will”) is revoked. Defendant contends that the 2023 Will was procured through the undue influence of Mr. John T. Harrington’s client, Liddy, and seeks to probate the 2019 Will. Plaintiff denies these allegations.

10. Plaintiff further requests that this Court admit the 2023 Will to probate and issue Letters Testamentary to Lydia A. Rosselli.

V. PRAYER

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff prays that Defendant be cited to appear and answer, that the Court declare the 2023 Will valid, and for such other and further relief to which she may be justly entitled.

Respectfully submitted,
/s/ John T. Harrington
John T. Harrington
Attorney for Plaintiff

title: Defendant’s Original Answer and Counterclaim to Contest Will
text:
IN THE PROBATE COURT NO. 2 OF DALLAS COUNTY, TEXAS

IN THE MATTER OF THE ESTATE OF
HENRY J. THORNTON, DECEASED

CAUSE NO. PR-24-00512

DEFENDANT’S ORIGINAL ANSWER AND COUNTERCLAIM TO CONTEST WILL

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

COMES NOW, CLIENT BEATRICE “BEA” THORNTON-KNOX, as defendant and counterclaimant, and files this Original Answer and Counterclaim to Contest Will, and respectfully shows:

I. PARTIES

1. Defendant/Counterclaimant, Bea Thornton-Knox (also known as Beatrice Thornton-Knox, Beatrice T. Knox, and to friends as “Bea”), is an individual residing in Dallas County, Texas. Her date of birth is July 22, 1975. Her Social Security number is 321-54-9876. She may be contacted at her counsel’s office.

2. Plaintiff, Marcus Anthony Thornton (formerly known as Marcus Anthony Thornton, Jr., and also referred to as Mark Thornton, M.A. Thornton, and Mr. Marcus Thornton), is an individual residing in Tarrant County, Texas, and is the opposing party who seeks to probate an alleged will dated January 10, 2024.

3. Counsel for Defendant: Michael R. Davidson, Davidson & Associates, 500 Elm Street, Dallas, Texas 75201. Telephone: 214-555-0293. Email: m.davidson@davidsonlaw.com.

4. Counsel for Plaintiff: Angela F. Reyes, Reyes Legal Group, P.C., 800 Oak Avenue, Fort Worth, Texas 76102.

5. The Honorable Linda S. Cho is the judge presiding over this matter.

II. JURISDICTION AND VENUE

6. Jurisdiction is proper under Tex. Est. Code § 55.002. Venue is proper in Dallas County because decedent Henry J. Thornton was domiciled here at death.

III. FACTUAL BACKGROUND

7. Decedent Henry J. Thornton died on September 5, 2024. Plaintiff offers a will dated January 10, 2024 (the “2024 Will”) which names Plaintiff as executor and sole beneficiary. Defendant contests this will, alleging it was executed under duress and that decedent lacked capacity. Defendant seeks to probate an earlier will dated March 20, 2019 (the “2019 Will”).

8. The minor child A.B. is a beneficiary under the 2019 Will. The case In re A.B., 789 S.W.3d 567 (Tex. App.—Dallas 2024) supports appointment of a guardian ad litem. Also, the court in Thornton v. Knox, 234 S.W.3d 890 (Tex. 2023) discussed duress issues. See also In re Estate of Moore, 456 S.W.3d 123 (Tex. 2019).

IV. DEFENSES AND COUNTERCLAIM

9. Defendant asserts that the 2024 Will is invalid due to undue influence exerted by Plaintiff. Defendant counterclaims for a declaratory judgment that the 2019 Will is the true last will.

V. PRAYER

WHEREFORE, Defendant prays that Plaintiff take nothing, that the 2019 Will be admitted to probate, and for all other relief.

Respectfully submitted,
/s/ Michael R. Davidson
Michael R. Davidson

title: Plaintiff’s Motion for Summary Judgment in Will Contest
text:
IN THE PROBATE COURT NO. 3 OF TRAVIS COUNTY, TEXAS

IN THE MATTER OF THE ESTATE OF
ROBERT L. WATERS, DECEASED

CAUSE NO. C-2024-0912

PLAINTIFF’S MOTION FOR SUMMARY JUDGMENT

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

COMES NOW, CLIENT JENNIFER L. WATERS-GARCIA, plaintiff herein, and moves for summary judgment on her claim to admit the Last Will and Testament of Robert L. Waters dated June 5, 2022, to probate. In support, she shows:

I. PARTIES

1. Plaintiff, Jennifer L. Waters-Garcia (also known as Jennifer Waters, Jenny Waters, J.L. Waters-Garcia, and Ms. Waters-Garcia), is an individual residing in Travis County, Texas. Her date of birth is March 12, 1983. Her Social Security number is 678 90 1234.

2. Defendant, Thomas Robert Waters (also known as Thomas R. Waters, Tom Waters, and Mr. T.R. Waters), is an individual residing in Williamson County, Texas, and is the opposing party contesting the will.

3. Counsel for Plaintiff: David H. Nguyen, Nguyen & Partners, 100 Congress Avenue, Austin, Texas 78701. Telephone: 512-555-0176. Email: d.nguyen@nguyenpartners.com.

4. Counsel for Defendant: Karen L. Smith, Smith Law Firm, 200 Brazos Street, Austin, Texas 78701.

5. The Honorable James T. Carter is the judge presiding.

II. ARGUMENT

6. The 2022 Will was properly executed under Tex. Est. Code § 251.051. Defendant’s allegations of undue influence are unsupported. The court in Waters v. Garcia, 890 S.W.3d 345 (Tex. App.—Austin 2024) held that similar claims require clear and convincing evidence. See also In re Estate of Brown, 567 S.W.3d 890 (Tex. 2022).

7. The minor A.B. is a contingent beneficiary, and this Court should protect her interests per In re A.B., 456 S.W.3d 678 (Tex. App.—Austin 2023).

III. PRAYER

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff requests summary judgment admitting the 2022 Will to probate.

Respectfully submitted,
/s/ David H. Nguyen

title: Order Appointing Guardian Ad Litem for Minor Beneficiary
text:
IN THE PROBATE COURT NO. 4 OF BEXAR COUNTY, TEXAS

IN THE MATTER OF THE ESTATE OF
CLARA M. ANDREWS, DECEASED

CAUSE NO. 2024-PR-00847

ORDER APPOINTING GUARDIAN AD LITEM FOR MINOR BENEFICIARY

On this day, the Court considered the need to protect the interests of the minor child A.B., a beneficiary under the Last Will and Testament of Clara M. Andrews, deceased.

The Court finds that A.B. is a minor and requires representation. It is therefore ORDERED that Elizabeth R. Torres, Attorney at Law, is appointed as Guardian Ad Litem for A.B., with all powers and duties under Tex. Est. Code § 53.101. The Court is guided by the principles in In re A.B., 345 S.W.3d 567 (Tex. App.—San Antonio 2022).

The parties in this will contest are: Plaintiff, GRACE ANDREWS-MILLER (also known as Grace Andrews, Grace M. Miller, G.A. Miller, and Ms. Andrews-Miller), who seeks to probate the will; and Defendant, RICHARD T. ANDREWS (also known as Richard Andrews, Dick Andrews, R.T. Andrews, and Mr. Andrews), who contests it.

Grace Andrews-Miller’s date of birth is November 5, 1978. Her Social Security number is 123-45-6789. Richard T. Andrews’ date of birth is August 19, 1975. His Social Security number is 987 65 4321.

Counsel for Plaintiff: Mark T. Benson, Benson Law Group, 300 Alamo Plaza, San Antonio, Texas 78205. Telephone: 210-555-0223. Email: m.benson@bensonlawgroup.com.

Counsel for Defendant: Cynthia R. Lopez, Lopez & Associates, 400 Riverwalk, San Antonio, Texas 78205.

The Honorable Michael S. Park is the judge presiding.

Dated: January 15, 2025.

/s/ Michael S. Park
JUDGE PRESIDING

title: Notice of Appeal in Will Contest
text:
IN THE COURT OF APPEALS FOR THE FIFTH DISTRICT OF TEXAS AT DALLAS

IN THE MATTER OF THE ESTATE OF
GEORGE F. HARRISON, DECEASED

TRIAL COURT CAUSE NO. PR-24-00336
APPELLATE DOCKET NO. 05-25-00123-CV

NOTICE OF APPEAL

TO THE HONORABLE JUSTICES OF SAID COURT:

COMES NOW, APPELLANT CLIENT PATRICIA L. HARRISON-DAVIS, appellant in the above-styled cause, and files this Notice of Appeal from the final judgment signed on March 1, 2025, by the Probate Court No. 5 of Dallas County.

I. PARTIES

1. Appellant, Patricia L. Harrison-Davis (also known as Patricia Harrison, Pat Harrison, P.L. Harrison-Davis, and Mrs. Harrison-Davis), is an individual residing in Dallas County, Texas. Her date of birth is June 30, 1972. Her Social Security number is 456-78-9012.

2. Appellee, Steven Michael Harrison (also known as Steven Harrison, Steve Harrison, S.M. Harrison, and Mr. Harrison), is the opposing party who successfully defended the will.

3. Counsel for Appellant: Robert J. Kim, Kim & Lee, P.C., 500 Main Street, Dallas, Texas 75202. Telephone: 214-555-0314. Email: r.kim@kimlee.com.

4. Counsel for Appellee: Laura B. Williams, Williams & Associates, 700 Commerce Street, Dallas, Texas 75202.

5. The trial judge was the Honorable David L. Adams.

II. BACKGROUND

6. This appeal arises from a will contest involving the estate of George F. Harrison. Appellant challenges the trial court’s admission of a will dated April 1, 2023. Appellant cites In re A.B., 678 S.W.3d 234 (Tex. App.—Dallas 2024) regarding the need for a guardian ad litem, and relies on Harrison v. Davis, 890 S.W.3d 456 (Tex. 2023) as controlling authority. See also In re Estate of Foster, 123 S.W.3d 789 (Tex. 2005).

7. The minor A.B. is a beneficiary under an earlier will.

III. PRAYER

WHEREFORE, Appellant requests that this Court reverse the trial court’s judgment and remand for a new trial.

Respectfully submitted,
/s/ Robert J. Kim
